Purpose: Where a human sees the system's current state and takes action on it.
Components & Technologies: dashboard.html (vanilla JS) with a shared apiFetch() wrapper; a React 19 + Vite console (frontend/) served same-origin at GET /console and GET /assets/*; login.html for sign-in.
Interactions: Talks to the backend only over its HTTP API (Layer 03); every request crosses Layer 02's session check first, never reaches Layer 04/05/06 directly.
Responsibilities: Render real system state, collect a human's approve/reject decision, and fail visibly (redirect to /login on a 401) rather than silently.
Significance: This is the layer a human operator actually trusts or distrusts the system through. Silent failure or stale data here undermines every layer working correctly beneath it.

Purpose: Blocks any action lacking real evidence, an allowed reversible type, or a genuine human approval, before an execution path is reachable.
Components & Technologies: remediationGuardrail.ts (pure, deterministic allow/deny); hitlQueue.ts (only the assigned approver may decide); auth/ (scrypt password hashing, sliding-expiry sessions, HttpOnly+SameSite=Strict cookies); rateLimiter.ts (login brute-force protection).
Interactions: Sits between Layer 01 and Layer 03 - every route except login/health runs through requireSession() first; Layer 03 calls into this layer's guardrail check before any execution path.
Responsibilities: Authenticate the human, authorize the specific action requested, and refuse anything failing either check deterministically, with no exceptions.
Significance: The entire governance model depends on this layer. Nothing with a real production effect crosses this boundary without a verified human approval - it is also what makes 'who is accountable' answerable.

Purpose: Sequences the actual workflow (detection, reasoning, escalation, notification) and holds the process-level state tying the other layers together.
Components & Technologies: monitoringService.ts, escalationService.ts, notificationService.ts (ntfy.sh delivery), reliability/circuitBreaker.ts, httpServer.ts (the route table).
Interactions: Receives requests from Layer 01 via Layer 02's gate; calls into Layer 04 for reasoning, Layer 05 for live data, and Layer 07 to record every step - the hub of the system.
Responsibilities: Every external call has an explicit timeout and capped retries; the circuit breaker trips after repeated upstream failure instead of hanging indefinitely.
Significance: This is where predictable behavior under failure gets decided. It contains a bad dependency's failure instead of letting it cascade through the rest of the system.

Purpose: Produces a root-cause explanation and confidence score from evidence gathered upstream - the one layer where an LLM actually reasons about system state.
Components & Technologies: rootCauseAgent.ts - real Anthropic Claude API calls (Claude Sonnet 5), zod-validated output; recommendationService.ts / cloudRecommendationService.ts turn a result into an evidence-linked recommendation.
Interactions: Called by Layer 03 with evidence from Layer 05; output flows back to Layer 03 for escalation and to Layer 02 as a proposed action. Never talks to Layer 01 or Layer 06 directly.
Responsibilities: Reason from real evidence to a real explanation with an honest confidence score; confidence below 60% auto-escalates rather than presenting a guess as settled.
Significance: The layer with the most inherent uncertainty in the system. It is allowed to be uncertain, but never allowed to decide whether to act on that uncertainty - that belongs to Layer 02, with a human behind it.

Purpose: Exposes the real data layer (SQL Server, Blob Storage) to the rest of the system safely - the boundary where untrusted external data first enters the system.
Components & Technologies: MCP Tool Gateway (mcpServerFactory.ts shared by index.ts's stdio transport and httpMcpServer.ts's bearer-token-gated, rate-limited StreamableHTTP transport); dmvLiveSource.ts, cloudBlobSource.ts, dmvReader.ts (live/fixture fallback).
Interactions: Called by Layer 03 (monitoring) and Layer 04's supporting services (evidence gathering); the only layer that talks directly to Layer 06's real infrastructure.
Responsibilities: Parameterized queries only; every live row is schema-validated (zod) before being trusted as evidence; read-only, least-privilege credentials only - structurally incapable of writing to a monitored system.
Significance: The trust boundary between data this system controls and data an external system handed it. Every injection, malformed-response, and credential-scope risk concentrates here.

Purpose: The real systems of record - where data actually lives, and the one process that serves everything else.
Components & Technologies: Azure SQL Database (monitored instance's system of record); Azure Blob Storage; a single mcp-server Node.js process serving the dashboard, console, and API, with no reverse proxy or container orchestration (a deliberate current-scale choice).
Interactions: Only Layer 05 talks to external systems of record directly; every other layer's persistent state (audit trail, sessions, rate limits, HITL queue) lives inside this same process, not in Azure SQL.
Responsibilities: Stay up, stay reachable, and be honest when it can't - every response tagged live or fallback rather than silently substituting one for the other.
Significance: Every claim the system makes ultimately rests on this layer. Honest live/fallback tagging is what keeps a quietly degraded dependency from silently collapsing the whole system's credibility.

Purpose: Makes the system's behavior reconstructable after the fact - not just current state, but what happened, when, and who decided it.
Components & Technologies: guardrails/auditLog.ts - immutable, idempotent-by-id entries, now persisted to an append-only JSONL file and rehydrated at startup (survives a restart, live-verified); observability/logger.ts (structured JSON logs); one correlation ID threaded through every service call.
Interactions: Every other layer writes into this one (Layer 02 records every decision, Layer 03 every cycle and escalation); this layer never calls back into any other layer - a sink, not a participant in the request path.
Responsibilities: Record every governance-relevant event exactly once (idempotent by id - a retried write is a safe no-op), never lose the record to a restart, and make it queryable by correlation ID.
Significance: Turns 'we have a guardrail' into 'we can prove the guardrail worked, on this date, for this decision, made by this person' - without a durable version of this layer, every other layer's governance logic is only as trustworthy as the last time someone happened to look.
